rule: Never author, fix, or revise what you grade — authoring mode is never grading mode; "I reviewed it while writing" is not a review.
WHAT is missing, never HOW to implement — product questions, never implementation questions; implementation detail, technical edge cases, architecture, and performance belong to later design work.

Not for: architecture/design review · code review (sole carve-out `mochiko:review-code-minimalism`, implement-side) · implementation planning · performance specs · no spec yet (`mochiko:authoring-requirements` first) · pre-spec enrichment of a sparse idea (`mochiko:analysis-iterative` — disjoint triggers by design).
An excess / unpaid-scope gap — no user need or ratified driver pays for it — is admissible only naming the driver it fails to trace to or the cheaper shape.
A floor- or NFR-derived obligation is never excess, however heavy it looks.
The feature layer is graded with the spec, same reviewer, same report — only the story-reader sees derivation dishonesty.
Scope creep is not a gap: clarify existing features, never add new ones as "missing requirements".
Coverage is complete, never sampled: every user story reviewed for completeness, every success criterion checked for measurability, edge cases hunted per main flow.
A regulatory or product-legal assertion is a floor-class external claim — verify per ../review-brainstorm/references/EXTERNAL-CLAIMS.md; undisclosed is a gap.
Grade staged feature-map writes against the git state of the map at run open, never a workspace copy.
Feature-map machinery is single-sourced in `mochiko:authoring-feature-map`; the feature-layer check list is the reviewer's mirror, never a second definition.
A UX-bearing spec has two legal Screens & Flows shapes: a SCR/FLOW manifest with its `prototype/` app, or the waiver line "No UX surface — prototype waived at intent".
Serve the prototype and click it (bun, or open `prototype/index.html`) — adversarial, not ceremonial: a skeptic walking the app finds what a text read cannot.
Check existing patterns and decisions first — never ask what is already answered.

The six requirement-defect classes — missing requirements · ambiguities · edge cases · assumption gaps · contradictions · excess / unpaid scope — are the canonical hunt taxonomy `devils-advocate` leans on; hunt them across the user-facing categories (user expectations · business rules · scope boundaries · success/failure states · permissions).
Implementation posture smuggled into a constraint ("files on disk" where the requirement is "locally computable") is an assumption-gap finding — it freezes a choice stakeholders never ratified.

Feature-layer Critical checks: derivation honesty (every feature traceable to supporting stories) · disposition completeness (every story homed to exactly one feature, or filter-rejected with the why recorded) · dedup by capability against the map files at baseline · delta legality (full grammar — what grows, in-flight mark, named spec; no `delivered` regressed) · SC re-homing (every SC-XXX on a verifying feature; deferred SCs and one-sided seams on the owning entry's obligations line) · in-flight handling (touches read into the owning spec; resolved by reference, sequenced delta, or escalation — never silent contradiction).

Feature-layer Important checks: granularity (one-breath capability, extent ≤ ~3 lines, or split) · entry well-formedness (entry-template shape, all fields) · selection-card honesty (deferred-SC list visible, agreeing with the SC split) · specs-index agreement (staged row matches staged writes — slug, FEAT-IDs, outcomes).
Prototype authority split: flows, screens, and data shown are binding; layout and styling advisory — a cosmetic finding against a low-fi prototype is wrong-altitude.

Screens & Flows Critical checks: screen reachability (every SCR-XXX renders a reachable page) · flow walkability (every FLOW-XXX clickable end-to-end, no dead ends) · scenario coverage (every P1 acceptance scenario has a FLOW click path) · flow traceability (every FLOW-XXX keyed to a real story scenario — no scope invention) · drift both directions (no page without a SCR row, no row without its page).

Screens & Flows Important checks: data-shape honesty (realistic fields/cardinality, enough to expose layout and flow problems) · FEAT tags (post-derivation rows FEAT-tagged; out-of-selection and filter-rejected screens greyed but reachable, rejected ones carrying the rejection pointer) · waiver second-guess (a waiver where stories imply screens, or a prototype the intent ruled out — graded against the Intent section's UX-bearing ruling).
Severity grammar: Critical = cannot build without this answer, ask now · Important = will cause rework, should ask now · Minor = polish, log and defer.
Density is never itself a gap (the `templates/artifact-format.md` envelope) — grade substance, never prose style; undisclosed overage past the envelope's size defaults is advisory per its rule 8.
Every question is a decision the stakeholder can make: 2–3 concrete options, what each means for users, why it matters — specific, never vague.
Never presuppose a mechanism in a question — "should we cache?" assumes caching.
Questions land in the Clarifications shape of `templates/advocate-report-template.md`, never a variant.

Report structure (machine-first findings YAML, clarifications with options + impact, recommended verdict, one-line `strengths:`) is single-sourced at `templates/advocate-report-template.md`; no report path named → same structure inline.
Verdict and per-finding dispositions land in the reviewed artifacts themselves — review evidence living only in conversation is a floor violation.
5–7 Critical/Important gaps per round, related gaps grouped — never a 20-gap dump.
The output is gap-finding input, never a clearing PASS/FAIL verdict of its own.
